method: Landscape from MPI 'New Frameworks for Language Access' (13 states + DC with cross-agency laws, Nov 2025), the California Little Hoover Commission brief (Aug 2026), NCIHC's legislation list (Jan 2024) and Wikipedia's official-language table. Each non-none state was then checked against statute, bill, session-law or agency text on official sites (DC Code, HRS, Minn. Stat., Md. Code, NRS, Mich. MCL, NJ DHS, NM HB 22, NYS OGS, WA session law, ORS, Del. Code, CO bills, MA/NC/PA pages). Web search quota ran out partway; see notes.

notes: Web-search quota ran out partway through. Every state marked none rests on the MPI table (13 states + DC, Nov 2025), the NCIHC list (Jan 2024), the CA Little Hoover Commission brief (Aug 2026) and spot checks, not on a state-by-state statute search. 2026 enactments after those trackers (like Washington's) may be missing.

Sector laws (court interpreters, health care, elections, 911, schools) were not canvassed state by state. Most states likely have court-interpreter rules or health-care provisions (NHeLP says every state had several health-care provisions as of 2019). Partial was assigned only to Oregon and Colorado for sector laws, because those surfaced in sources read; other states may deserve partial.

Delaware is unclear: 29 Del. C. ch. 106 (2024) is a sampled-agency reporting and housing-assistance law that expires Sept. 30, 2026 per the Code. The Code page still showed the expiry notice on 2026-11-02 and no extension was found. MPI lists Delaware as cross-agency.

Washington's 2026 law (SHB 2475, Ch. 142) is rated partial because it sets policy, guidelines (due 12/1/2027) and agency reports (6/30/2028) rather than a direct service mandate, and states it creates no new rights. Reviewers may prefer enacted.

MPI counts MA (EO 615), NC (Governor's Office policy) and DE as cross-agency. Here MA and NC are partial (executive action, no statute found) and DE is unclear. Pennsylvania (EO 2024-01 plus a 2025 program) is not on MPI's list; its EO text was not retrieved, only a state press release.

Pending bills: no state without a law was confirmed to have a live bill. MA H.3384 and S.2622 sit in Ways and Means (last action Oct 2025) but MA is already partial. CT bills (2025 HB 6477, SB 955; 2026 HB 5347) show no action past a chamber calendar. DE HB 302 (government websites) sits in House Appropriations. Bills in states not checked may exist.

Year conventions: Hawaii 2006 (MPI, NCIHC) although the chapter was recodified as 321C by L 2012 c 201; Maryland 2002 per NCIHC and the 2002 bill (MPI says 2003); NJ 2024 is the signing year (P.L. 2023, c.263); Michigan 2023 acts took effect Feb. 28, 2024.

Access problems: capitol.hawaii.gov, nysenate.gov, mass.gov and California's leginfo blocked automated fetches; text came from data.capitol.hawaii.gov, NewYork.Public.Law plus the NY OGS page, a press release, and CalHR plus a university mirror of the statute. ilga.gov failed TLS checks in curl, so Illinois Act text was read through the fetch tool; the quote comes from the Governor's ONA page.
Official-English status comes from Wikipedia's state table (secondary, may be dated; for example it shows Ohio and Texas as no). Official-English laws are noted in x but did not change any status.

NM: the enrolled bill (final PDF) was read to confirm the new subsection (11); the quote is taken from the HTML bill page because the PDF has line numbers inside the phrase. The signing (Ch. 18) comes from LegiScan only.
